title: The Brown adjoint of $Rf_!$ on the localizing category

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal T_X$, $\mathcal D=\mathcal T_Y$. In the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], $Y$ is separated and of finite type over $k$. The final sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] therefore makes $Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The same setting supplies a compactification $c=(j,p)$, with the quasi-compactness of $j$ included in the definition [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. The statement of [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] therefore applies to this $c$: $F_c=Rp_*D(j_!):\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is exact and preserves all set-indexed direct sums. The assumed compact generation gives the source condition for Brown. At $Y$, [sk-lem-brown-hypotheses] supplies the locally small triangulated target and its direct sums. Thus both Hom groups and all coproducts used below exist in the fixed size convention.

source.place: Part (1), exactness and direct-sum preservation before the Brown application.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-brown-representability-right-adjoint] to $F_c:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$. Step 1 checks every hypothesis: both categories are triangulated with set-indexed coproducts, $\mathcal C$ is compactly generated, and $F_c$ is exact and preserves these coproducts. Obtain a functor $G_c:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ and an adjunction $F_c\dashv G_c$. Set $f_c^!=G_c$. Its adjunction bijection is the one in clause (1), natural in both $M$ and $N$, and let $\varepsilon^c_N:F_cG_cN\to N$ denote its counit. This applies Brown only on $\mathcal C$, not on the ambient category of all pro-étale complexes. The cited criterion is exactly Stacks 0A8G (proposition-brown), whose proof applies 0A8F to $M\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F_cM,N)$ and assembles its representing objects.

Write $F=F_c$, $G=G_c$, and $\xi^n_M:F(M[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(FM)[n]$ for the coherent shifts of $F$. For each integer $n$ and $N$, the natural chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,(GN)[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M[-n],GN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F(M[-n]),N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FM,N[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,G(N[n]))$$
is a bijection. Both its ends are representable presheaves on $\mathcal C$, so the full-faithfulness statement [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] gives a unique natural isomorphism $\alpha^n_N:(GN)[n]\xrightarrow{\sim}G(N[n])$. This uses only transformations between representables, not the general evaluation form of Yoneda. Its transpose is $\varepsilon_N[n]\circ\xi^n_{GN}$, so
$$\varepsilon_{N[n]}\circ F(\alpha^n_N)=\varepsilon_N[n]\circ\xi^n_{GN}.$$
Naturality in $N$ follows by transposing the naturality square and using naturality of $\varepsilon$ and $\xi^n$. Under the shift associators, $\alpha^0$ is the identity, and the transpose of $\alpha^n_{N[m]}\circ(\alpha^m_N)[n]$ is $\varepsilon_N[m+n]\circ\xi^{m+n}_{GN}$: substitute the displayed counit identity twice, move $F$ past each shift by $\xi$, and use the coherence of $\xi$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives the composition law for $\alpha^{m+n}$. Finally, if $\eta$ is the unit, transposing $G(\xi^n_M)\circ\eta_{M[n]}$ gives $\xi^n_M$ by the triangle identity. Transposing $\alpha^n_{FM}\circ(\eta_M)[n]$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{(FM)[n]}\circ F(\alpha^n_{FM})\circ F((\eta_M)[n])
=(\varepsilon_{FM}\circ F\eta_M)[n]\circ\xi^n_M=\xi^n_M.$$
Thus these maps agree. This is exactly unit compatibility with the shifts; the preceding displayed counit identity is counit compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact, construction of the adjunction-induced shift; coherence and unit square expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-triangulated-right-adjoint] to $F_c\dashv G_c$, using the exactness of $F_c$ from step 1 and the coherent shifts and unit/counit compatibility from step 3. Its conclusion states that $G_c$ is exact with these specified shift isomorphisms. This proves clause (2). The correct general exact-adjoint tag is 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact); 0A8G is the Brown criterion used in step 2.

source.place: Tag 0A8D, lemma-adjoint-is-exact; Mathlib formulation with compatible shifts.

proof.text:
For a second right adjoint $J$ of this same $F_c$, with counit $\varepsilon^J$, use [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]. It gives the natural isomorphism $\gamma:G_c\xrightarrow{\sim}J$ whose component is the $J$-transpose of $\varepsilon^c_N$. In particular
$$\varepsilon^J_N\circ F_c(\gamma_N)=\varepsilon^c_N.$$
The cited statement gives the inverse by the opposite transpose and uniqueness even among arbitrary counit-compatible families. Compatibility with the full adjunction bijections follows directly: the transpose of $\gamma_N\circ a$, for $a:M\to G_cN$, is $\varepsilon^J_N\circ F_c(\gamma_N)\circ F_c(a)=\varepsilon^c_N\circ F_c(a)$. Thus the uniqueness is precisely adjunction-compatible uniqueness, not uniqueness among all natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Part (3), uniqueness for two right adjoints of one compact-support functor.

proof.text:
For compactifications $c_1,c_2$, [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] gives $\phi_{21}:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2$, independent of refinements, with $\phi_{cc}=1$ and $\phi_{32}\phi_{21}=\phi_{31}$. Precomposition with $\phi_{21,M}$ followed by the adjunction for $F_1$ gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_2M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(F_1M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_1N).$$
This is natural in $M,N$, so it transfers the adjunction to $F_2\dashv G_1$, with counit $\varepsilon^1_N\circ\phi_{21,G_1N}^{-1}$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to this transferred adjunction and $F_2\dashv G_2$, obtaining the unique $\gamma_{21}:G_1\xrightarrow{\sim}G_2$ satisfying
$$\varepsilon^2_N\circ F_2(\gamma_{21,N})=\varepsilon^1_N\circ\phi_{21,G_1N}^{-1}.$$
For three compactifications, naturality of $\phi_{32}^{-1}$ and the two counit equations give
$$\varepsilon^3_N\circ F_3(\gamma_{32,N}\gamma_{21,N})
=\varepsilon^2_N\circ F_2(\gamma_{21,N})\circ\phi_{32,G_1N}^{-1}
=\varepsilon^1_N\circ\phi_{21,G_1N}^{-1}\circ\phi_{32,G_1N}^{-1}
=\varepsilon^1_N\circ\phi_{31,G_1N}^{-1}.$$
Uniqueness therefore gives $\gamma_{32}\gamma_{21}=\gamma_{31}$; for $c_1=c_2$ it gives $\gamma_{cc}=1$. This proves the independence and coherence assertions in clause (3).
